props.text: Nobody can price an implant case from a phone call. Here is what actually moves the number.
By the practice, on your behalf
All five come out of the consultation and the 3D scan.
One tooth, a span, or an entire arch. Four posts carrying an arch is usually more cost-effective than replacing each tooth individually.
How long they have been missing
Bone recedes where teeth are not loading it. Time gone is the biggest predictor of whether anything has to be rebuilt first.
Extractions, bone grafting, sinus work: separate procedures with their own healing time, and the usual reason two quotes are months and thousands apart.
A zirconia fixed prosthesis is not the same object as an acrylic one. What is being quoted matters as much as how many implants.
Surgery, restoration and the laboratory under one roof removes the margin each outside party adds, and the second set of appointments with it.
Second opinions on implant surgery are free here. Bring the plan and the scan, and you will get a straight read on what is in it.
The cheapest option on day one is rarely the cheapest option.
are the lowest number at the start, and not a long-term solution: they rest on gum tissue, they move, they need relining, and the bone underneath keeps receding because nothing is loading it.
sit in the middle. The denture clips onto implants, which stops the movement and puts load back into the bone.

are the highest number up front and the lowest maintenance afterwards: no relining, no adhesive, no nightly removal. Ask any practice quoting you what the ten-year cost looks like, not just the day-one one.

Most dental PPO plans are accepted. Coverage for implants is often limited, but limited is not nothing. The practice files the claims on your behalf and works the plan for every benefit it actually entitles you to.
Three lenders, for three different situations.
Monthly payment plans through partners the practice already works with. Apply directly with any of them.
Flexible monthly payment options for patients who qualify. Manage the treatment cost over a term instead of in one payment.
, at fair fixed rates. The longest term of the three.
Apply from a phone in minutes, choose the rate, term and payment that fit, and have funds sent to your account for a lower APR.
Why is there no price list on this page?
Because an honest one cannot exist. Two people missing the same tooth can need entirely different treatment depending on what the bone is doing. You get a real number after the scan, in writing.

Some plans offer limited coverage. The practice files claims on your behalf and works to get every benefit your plan entitles you to. Whether that is a large or small share depends entirely on the plan.
Can I finance the whole case?
In most cases yes, through CareCredit, Proceed Finance or LendingClub. Proceed Finance carries the longest terms of the three, up to 96 months.
Is a second opinion really free?
Yes, on implant surgery. If you have been quoted elsewhere, bring the plan and any imaging.

props.text: The ones patients actually ask, including the two about pain and money.
Implants are the most complete answer to tooth loss there is, and the most involved process. Which is why they raise more questions.
What an implant is, and whether it works.

Three parts: a titanium or ceramic post, an abutment, and a restoration. The post functions as a tooth root does, and what sits on top can be a single crown, a bridge, a denture or a full-arch prosthesis.
Why are implants called the gold standard?

They are the only permanent tooth replacement option, and they are designed to last decades. Because the post is placed into the jawbone, the health benefits are comparable to a natural tooth, which is not true of anything resting on the gum.

Consistently over 95% since implants were introduced decades ago. That figure comes from surgical technology, materials, clinical experience and long-term maintenance. The last one is yours to supply.

Many patients already are, and many of the rest qualify after bone grafting or extractions. Candidacy is determined accurately only after a comprehensive consultation and evaluation, not from a web page.
The surgery, the pain, and the recovery.

Often completed in a few hours using patient-fitted surgical guides, planned from the scan beforehand. How long yours takes depends on several factors; you will be comfortable regardless of the answer.
The surgery is completed under sedation. You will feel no pain, and you stay relaxed throughout.
Rest for a few days. Patients generally report minor discomfort that over-the-counter medication handles, and most return to normal activity after about a week. A
soft food diet is required for the next several months
while the implants integrate. That part is not optional, and it is the one people underestimate.
How long does the whole process take?
Anywhere from a few months to over a year. Bone grafting, if you need it, is a separate procedure with several months of healing first. After placement, integration takes
before the final restoration is attached, and in many cases you wear a temporary in the meantime.
Precision at placement is what decides the outcome fifteen years later.
How do I care for dental implants?
Like natural teeth, with no special maintenance. Brush twice a day and floss once. Some restorations want a water flosser to clear debris from underneath.
Yes, and this surprises people. Implant restorations cannot decay, but they can develop
, an infection of the gums around the implant, caused by plaque exactly as gum disease is. Keep the six-month visits.
They are designed to last decades and have the potential to last the rest of your life. Surgical technology, clinical experience and your own habits all affect it.

It depends on how many teeth are missing and for how long, the materials, and what has to happen first. Nobody can give you a real number before an evaluation. The practice helps you apply for financing and files insurance claims for you.
Anatomy, the four options, the process and the cases.
Three tiers at 20%, 60% and over 98% of natural function.

props.text: Ten everyday complaints, and what is actually done about each one.
Do you cover your mouth when you smile?
Most of this is straightforward to treat. Some of it is not cosmetic at all: bleeding gums and constant bad breath are early gum disease.
Ten things people come in with.
Open the one that sounds like yours.

Jawbone recession lets a denture come loose, and a loose denture rubs. The fix is anchorage: implant-supported dentures or full-arch implants, fixed into the jaw and strong enough to eat normally with.

bad breath, alongside gums that bleed and teeth that loosen, is gum disease, and untreated it aggravates diabetes, high blood pressure and cardiovascular disease. Treated with customized gum disease therapy.

The earliest sign of gum disease. Tartar releases bacteria, the gums redden, swell and recede, and advanced gum disease eventually stops being curable. Surgical and non-surgical treatments both exist; an evaluation settles which.
Once a tooth is broken open, bacteria get inside and the infection can end in root canal therapy. Treated with a filling, bonding, an inlay, an onlay or a crown, depending on how much tooth is left.
Not only cosmetic. Misaligned teeth hold plaque where a brush cannot reach, and they skew the bite, which shows up as jaw discomfort rather than as an aesthetic complaint.

Red, receding or tender gums, and pockets forming between gum and tooth. Untreated it leads to tooth loss and jawbone recession, and is linked to respiratory disease, diabetes, pregnancy complications, heart disease, stroke and cancer.
Gums frame the teeth, and the proportion between the two is most of what makes a smile look right. Precise recontouring rebalances the gumline, usually in a single visit.

Without a root stimulating it, the bone under the empty socket deteriorates, and it spreads, which is how one lost tooth becomes the neighboring ones. Bridges and implants both restore the smile; only implants protect the jaw.

The tooth is X-rayed, so what is happening inside the enamel is visible rather than guessed at, and the aim is always to keep the natural tooth. Wisdom teeth aside, an extracted tooth should be replaced.
A full set of healthy teeth can still be a smile someone hides. Professional whitening handles it, and the shade is chosen with you rather than set once.
It is very often smaller than you have been assuming.
Several of these are the same problem.
Bad breath, bleeding gums and gum disease are one condition at three stages. Missing teeth, loose dentures and most of the toothache list are one consequence of another.
A prosthodontist is trained to see the whole mouth as one system, so the useful question is not
what do I do about this tooth

props.text: Written out in full, because a guarantee you cannot read is not much of a guarantee.
Any part that fails inside five years is replaced free of charge.

That is the whole of it, and it is the sentence the practice has published since before this site was built. Replacement is free of charge: no deductible, no pro-rata scale that pays less in year four than in year one, and no charge for the appointment at which the replacement is fitted.
The implant work this practice carries out is covered for five years. The post is designed as a lifetime replacement root; the parts above it are what a warranty is for.
Veneers, crowns and the rest of the cosmetic work designed and fitted here are covered on the same five-year terms.
A full arch carries the warranty too, on the same condition as everything else: the six-monthly Precare cleanings.

htmlAttributes.alt: A patient and clinician talking through a treatment plan

props.text: Precare: a cleaning every six months.

The warranty is conditional on Precare, the practice's own maintenance program: general cleanings every six months. That is the same interval any set of teeth needs, and it is the only condition attached.

The reason is not administrative. What ends most implant work early is not the implant, it is the gum and bone around it, and six-monthly cleaning is what catches that while it is still reversible. A practice that guarantees its work for five years needs to see the work during those five years.
A general cleaning every six months
Booked at the office that did the work
Keeps the five-year warranty in force
Call the office that did the work.

There is no form and no claims department. Ring the office, describe what has happened, and you will be seen. Second opinions on implant surgery are free, whether the original work was done here or somewhere else.
How long does the warranty run?
Five years from the date the work is fitted.
What does “replaced free of charge” mean?
The failed part is remade and refitted at no cost to you. The laboratory is in the building, which is why the practice is able to commit to this at all.
What keeps the warranty in force?
The Precare cleanings, every six months. That is the condition the practice publishes, and the only one.
My question is not answered here.
Call the office rather than assume. The practice would rather answer a specific question about your own treatment than have this page guess at it.
